label: EDPB Guidelines 01/2022 — Right of Access (Art. 15)
body: • Access is a broad default: provide all data, all categories, all recipients. Restrictions are exceptional and must be specifically justified.
• Identity verification (Art. 12(6)): proportionate to risk — don't demand more ID than needed. Re-use existing authentication where possible.
• "Copy" of personal data under Art. 15(3) is a full and accurate reproduction — not a summary, not aggregated.
• Multiple requests / "abusive" claims (Art. 12(5)): high bar — controller bears the burden of demonstrating manifestly unfounded or excessive character.
• Third-party data protection (Art. 15(4)): narrow exception — redaction is preferred over withholding the response. Don't refuse the entire request because some data implicates third parties.
• Format: commonly used electronic form when the request is electronic, unless subject requests otherwise.
• Layered approach: a structured summary + the underlying data + Art. 15(1) information is the best practice format.
Scope note: EDPB guidance adopted after Brexit has no status under the UK GDPR — for UK SARs, use the ICO Right of Access guidance.
